1

 Judgment

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- on account of the death of Sri. Venkatesh, in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, is as follows:
On 6.1.2024 at about 12.10 p.m. to 12.15 p.m. the deceased Venkatesh was crossing the road opposite of Magnolia Layout, Kadumane cross, Shanumangala road, Bidadi Hobli, Ramanagara, at that time the driver of crane bearing No.KA-51-P-8307 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.
Due to the impact, the deceased fell down and struck under the said vehicle and the left side wheel ran over the head of the deceased and the deceased succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
The petitioners have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses, funeral, death ceremonies and other expenses.

At the time of accident, the deceased was doing incense sticks business as peddler and earning Rs.20,000/- to Rs.30,000/- per month and he was contributing his entire income for the maintenance of his family.
Due to the untimely death of deceased the petitioner has suffered mentally and physically and lost his father.
The petitioner is the son of deceased.
The respondents are the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondent No.2 owner remained absent and placed exparte.
The Respondent No.1 insurance company appeared and filed written statement by denying the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the crane bearing No.KA- 51-P-8307.
Further contended that, at the time of accident the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence.
The accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of deceased himself and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further denied the age,
avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation has claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence the respondent No.1 prays to dismiss the petition against it.
4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court at the time of judgment:

sentences.text:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of crane bearing Reg. No. KA-51-P-8307 by its driver, in RTA took place on 6.1.2024 at about 12.10 p.m. opposite Magnolia Layout,
Kadumane corss, Shanumangala road, Bidadi Hobli, Ramangara?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
4 . What order or award?

Recasted Issue No.1;
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that deceased Venkatesh K. died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 6.1.2024 at about 12.10 p.m.

Opposite Magnolia Layout, Kadumane cross,
Shanumangala road, Bidadi Hobli, Ramanagara, due to the rash and negligence driving of the crane bearing Reg. No. KA-51-P-8307 by its driver?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.
The respondents have not adduced any evidence.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the material evidence that is available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.
Recasted issue No.1: Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per final orders for the following.-

REASONS RECASTED ISSUE NO.1:
8.

The petitioner to prove his claim has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, IMV report, IMV reply, IMV inspection report, inquest report, PM report and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 10.
9.
As per the documents, Ex.P1 FIR is came to be registered on the basis of the information given by one Govindaraju as per Ex.P2 who is an eye witness to the accident.
The first informant being the eye witness alleged the rash and negligent driving by the driver of crane bearing No. KA-51-P-8307.
After registration of Fir the spot mahazar and rough sketch was conducted by the IO wherein it shows that the accident spot is within 12 feet from the divider.
The Ex.P5 is IMV report.
It is very important to note that the alleged accident is caused while the deceased was trying to cross the road.

The accident is not seriously disputed by the respondent No.1.
10.
The respondent No.1 insurance company has denied the fact of negligence by the driver of crane bearing No. KA-51-P-8307.
The owner of the crane bearing No. KA-51-P-8307 is also made as respondent No.2 in this case.

The respondent No.2 remained absent and not chosen to deny the Seena vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197720424/
3 allegation of negligence from his driver.

sentences.text: The respondents does not chosen to examine the driver of the crane who is an eye witness and who is the better person to depose regarding the fact of negligence.
The respondent No.1 insurance company also not chosen to lead the evidence.
The fact of accident is not denied by the respondent No.1.
Only the fact of negligence by the driver of crane bearing No. KA-51-P- 8307 is disputed.

It is the contention of respondent No.1 that even though the crane was proceeding slowly by following the traffic rules, the victim/ deceased was crossing the highway without their being any crossing zone, zebra crossing and no signal lights and suddenly entered into the road.

11. Hence, this tribunal has to examine the fact of negligence with the evidence of PW.1, police documents along with the contentions raised by the respondent No.1 about the contributory negligence by the deceased.
12. Admittedly, the PW.1 is not an eye witness.
There is no evidence from the respondent in support of their contention.
If we perused the contents of Ex.P.3 mahazar and rough sketch the accident exact spot is within 12 feet of the divider.
In the FIR itself it is alleged that the deceased was crossing the road and dashed by the crane.
The accident spot is near to the middle side divider which shows that the deceased was crossing the road.
As per the mahazar from the accident spot after 20 feet the crane is stopped and as per Ex.P4 rough sketch, from the accident spot there is a 40 feet to a electric pole which is on the divider.
After the crane the divider is open which shows that where the divider is opened and vehicles and persons are permitted to cross the road.
Thus, it is evident that the deceased was crossing the road in the middle of the highway.

The PW.1 at the time of cross-examination has deposed that as there was a construction of road, his father crossed the road in the middle of the highway, but the said contention cannot be accepted because, as per Ex.P3 mahazar and Ex.P4 rough sketch, the two way traffic movement is shown.
Thus, it is evident t hat the deceased was crossing the road where it was not permitted to cross the highway.

In the judgment reported in ILR 2003 Kar 1104 between Koosappa Poojary V/s. K. Sadabba and others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held as follows;
" All the more so the driver of the vehicle ought to have been more prudent and circumspect while driving. But, it cannot be lost sight of the fact that a duty is also cast on a pedestrian and he should use due care and caution in going upon and crossing the road and it is his duty to look out for oncoming traffic.

entities.text: Koosappa Poojary V/s. K. Sadabba and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insofar as the another duty cast on the pedestrian is concerned, it is needless to say that he has to give the driver a plenty of time to see him and slow down and start before he attempts to cross or put one foot on the crossing,
It is not always necessary that the vehicular traffic will have to stop for a pedestrian to cross, for the vehicle needs more time to stop in view of the speed a motor generates.

Moreover, whenever a pedestrian is crossing over a roadway at any place other than which is meant for pedestrian crossing, they cannot claim any specific precedence and the responsibility for causing the accident more often than not will have to be shared by the pedestrian along with the vehicle driver.
In view of this, it cannot be said that it was only the driver of the vehicle in question was solely responsible for the accident.

It has also to be noted that Seena vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197720424/
4 there is no evidence forthcoming to show that it was the pedestrian crossing or whether there were any zebra-crossing.

sentences.text:
In view of the fact that the claimant had crossed the road where he was not supposed to cross certain degree of contributory negligence will have to be attributed to him."
13.
No doubt that the pedestrians has to cross the road in the place where it is meant for pedestrian crossing.
In this case.
From the accident spot nearly after 40 feet where the divider was opened and the pedestrians are required to cross the road in the said place.
Thus, the deceased was crossing the road in the middle of the highway instead of crossing the road in the nearby divider open has certainly contributed towards the cause of accident.
But it is very important to note that the accident is caused by the crane.
The crane is an heavy vehicle and expected to move in very slow manner and the divider should be in controllable speed.
On perusal of the Ex.P2 first information, it is alleged that the left side wheel of the crane was ran over on the deceased.
This shows that the crane being the heavy vehicle was not in a controllable speed in a crowded place.
The driver of crane has to be in a controllable speed to control his heavy vehicle.
The nature of the injuries found on the body as per Ex.P3, Ex.P8 inquest and Ex.P9 post mortem shows that the driver of crane was not in a controllable speed and was negligent.
This shows that merely because the deceased was crossing the road in the middle of the highway and if the driver of crane was in a controllable speed, he could have control his heavy vehicle.
As such, the negligence of the driver of the crane is more vigilant than the negligence of the deceased.
Hence, the contributory negligence of 10% is attributed towards the deceased and remaining negligence is on the part of the driver of the crane.
Accordingly issue No.1 answered in the partly affirmative.
ISSUE NO.2 14.

As held herein above, the petitioner proved that Venkatesh died on 6.1.2024 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by respondent No.2.
15.
As contended in the petition the petitioner is the son of the deceased Venkatesh.
The respondents do not specifically deny the relationship of petitioner with deceased.
The petitioner to prove his relationship with the deceased, has produced the notarized copies of Aadhaar cards of petitioner and deceased which are marked under Ex.P.11.
During the course of recording the evidence the notarized copies of Aadhar cards are compared with the original documents and found correct.
In the Ex.P8 inquest also the photograph of the petitioner is available with the body of deceased and he being the son has given statement by identifying the body of his deceased father.
16. As per these documents the petitioner is the son of the deceased, but the respondents do not dispute the relationship of the petitioner with deceased.
The respondents have not adduced any evidence to disprove the relationship of the petitioner with the deceased.
17. In the absence of contradictory evidence the evidence of the petitioner is to be accepted and it is considered that, petitioner is the son of the deceased.
At the time of cross-examination the contention is raised by the respondent No.1 insurance company that the petitioner being the major son is not entitled for compensation.

In this regard, the learned counsel for the petitioner has relied Seena vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197720424/
5 on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356 between National Ins.
Co. Ltd., V/s. Birender and others, wherein it is held as follows;
"It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation. Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependant on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.

In the High Court of Punjab and Hariyana at Chadigarh in FAO No.1007 and 1008 /2014 dated 10-02- 2020 between Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Vipanjit Kaur and others No doubt, the son is aged around 48 years and working in the Air Force while the daughter is aged around 42 years and her husband is posted as a Sub Inspector in the Punjab Police and both of them are thus having their own independent sources of income.

No doubt, both the claimants are grown up and self- dependent but that does not mean or can be construed that they did not suffer any loss on account of sudden loss of both of their parents.

It has been rightly contended by learned counsel for the respondents/claimants that son and the daughter with the death of their parents have lost protection, physical as well as psychological, besides sense of fulfillment of having parents to look after and cater to their daily requirements of life and emotional support.

No doubt, the parents were senior citizens but one has to take a realistic approach that they would certainly be looking after Seena vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197720424/

. By this loss the family has lost companionship, and the pain and agony that has accompanied this sudden loss can never be compensated in terms of money.
One cannot ignore the fact that Surinder Kaur even in her advance age would be contributing her lot in the household chores, cooking food, cleaning and such like daily duties.

The family claims to be having agricultural land besides having milching cattle and therefore, in rural household it is a matter of common knowledge that women contribute towards looking after the cattle and agricultural produce and contribute their lot towards the source of earning from these fields.

The learned Tribunal has lost sight of the fact in not awarding compensation on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, which are handsomely part of calculations in such claim petitions.

Since there is no division of heads under which various amounts of compensation has been awarded, but having an overall look at the total compensation awarded in case of each of the deceased being ` 4.52 lacs and ` 3.50 lacs in lump sum and considering what has been left out as detailed in the foregoing lines, keeping in view the prevalent price index, there is no overwhelming occasion for this Court to show indulgence and thus this Court does not feel that the amount so awarded could be in any manner termed to be excessive necessitating intervention by this Court and rather appears to be just and appropriate in the prevalent scenario.
In the light of the same, the impugned award does not call for any interference and both the present appeals as such are disposed of as dismissed.
18. By applying the above precedent merely because the petitioner is the major son of the deceased his application cannot be rejected.

In this case also, as per the evidence available on record the deceased and the petitioner is working as labourers and the deceased was selling Agarbathis which shows that their earning was meagre income.
As such, they are certainly dependents on each other.
Accordingly, in this case the petitioner being a major son is entitled for the compensation in accordance with his dependency.
19. Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.
As per the Aadhaar card of the deceased produced as per Ex.P11- the date of birth of the deceased is shown as 03.10.1954.
The accident took place on 06.01.2024.
Thus, as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 70 years.
20. As stated in the petition deceased was doing the selling of incense sticks ( Agarbathi business as peddler) and earning Rs.20,000/- to Rs.30,000/- per month.
To prove the said fact, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
But the mahazar discloses that along with the body of the deceased they have found incense sticks bag.
This shows that the deceased was working as stated in the petition, but the income of the deceased is not established.

Hence, in the absence of material evidence, the notional income of the deceased is considered at Rs.16,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2024 and the annual income comes to Rs.1,98,000/-.
21.
As per Sarala varma case the proper multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is 5.

Since the deceased left his son, it is considered that, there is only one dependent of deceased, hence half of the income is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, then the total loss of dependency would be Seena vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197720424/
7 Rs.4,95,000/- (Rs.16,500/- X 12 X 5= Rs.9,90,000/- minus half of the income i.e., =
Rs.4,95,000/-).

Pranay Sethi & others), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "While determining the income, in case the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

sentences.text: An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
23. This citation is not applicable to the case on hand since the age of the deceased is 70 years.

24. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:
In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130, the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".

25. This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.
26.

The Petitioner being the son is entitled for sum of Rs.44,000/- ( Rs.44,000/-. Rs.40,000/x 10%
hike every three years from 2017 as per Pranay Sethi Case) under the head of loss of consortium.

27. Further I inclined to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of love and affection, Rs.16,500/-
towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 4,95,000/-
2. Loss of future prospects NIL 3. Loss of consortium Rs. 44,000/-
4. Towards loss of love and Rs. 50,000/-

Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500/-

28 . As per the reasons discussed in Issue No.1 it is held that the deceased also contributed 10% of negligence towards the cause of accident.

Hence if the 10% of contributory negligence is deducted then the total amount of Rs.6,22,000/- (
Rs.6,22,000/- - Rs.62,200/-
= 5,59,800) which is rounded off to Rs.5,60,000/- is entitled to be payable to the petitioner as compensation.
29. Liability:- The respondent No.1 in its objection statement has denied the issuance of policy to the crane bearing No. KA-51-P-8307.
But the respondent No.1 insurance company has not lead any evidence in support of his defence.

PW.1 during his oral evidence and at the time of filing of petition the copy of the policy is filed along with the petition which shows that the Crane bearing No.
KA-51-P-8307 was duly insured with the respondent No.1 insurance company for the period of 12- 07-2023 to 11-07-2024.
The date of accident is 06-01- 2024.
Further no grounds are made out by showing the violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.2 owner.
In the charge sheet also no offences are invoked against the driver of the Crane bearing No. KA-51-P-8307 for driving the said vehicle without having licence.
Hence, the said defence of the respondent No.1 cannot be acceptable.

Accordingly, the respondent No.1 insurance company shall indemnify the respondent No.2 and they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.4:-
30.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,60,000/- (Rupees Five lakhs sixty thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
By considering the quantum of compensation, office is directed to release the entire share of petitioner by taking necessary vouchers and documents.

Moreover, whenever a pedestrian is crossing over a roadway at any place other than which is meant for pedestrian crossing, they cannot claim any specific precedence and the responsibility for causing the accident more often than not will have to be shared by the pedestrian along with the vehicle driver.
In view of this, it cannot be said that it was only the driver of the vehicle in question was solely responsible for the accident.
The nature of the injuries found on the body as per Ex.P3, Ex.P8 inquest and Ex.P9 post mortem shows that the driver of crane was not in a controllable speed and was negligent.
This shows that merely because the deceased was crossing the road in the middle of the highway and if the driver of crane was in a controllable speed, he could have control his heavy vehicle.
As such, the negligence of the driver of the crane is more vigilant than the negligence of the deceased.
Hence, the contributory negligence of 10% is attributed towards the deceased and remaining negligence is on the part of the driver of the crane.
The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short, 'the Act') admittedly is a welfare statute for the betterment of the claimants.
their grand- children for their nurturing, psychological and physical well-being, and would be a source of joy and happiness for the entire family
. By this loss the family has lost companionship, and the pain and agony that has accompanied this sudden loss can never be compensated in terms of money.
One cannot ignore the fact that Surinder Kaur even in her advance age would be contributing her lot in the household chores, cooking food, cleaning and such like daily duties.
The family claims to be having agricultural land besides having milching cattle and therefore, in rural household it is a matter of common knowledge that women contribute towards looking after the cattle and agricultural produce and contribute their lot towards the source of earning from these fields.
Since there is no division of heads under which various amounts of compensation has been awarded, but having an overall look at the total compensation awarded in case of each of the deceased being ` 4.52 lacs and ` 3.50 lacs in lump sum and considering what has been left out as detailed in the foregoing lines, keeping in view the prevalent price index, there is no overwhelming occasion for this Court to show indulgence and thus this Court does not feel that the amount so awarded could be in any manner termed to be excessive necessitating intervention by this Court and rather appears to be just and appropriate in the prevalent scenario.
In the light of the same, the impugned award does not call for any interference and both the present appeals as such are disposed of as dismissed.
18. By applying the above precedent merely because the petitioner is the major son of the deceased his application cannot be rejected.
In this case also, as per the evidence available on record the deceased and the petitioner is working as labourers and the deceased was selling Agarbathis which shows that their earning was meagre income.
Accordingly, in this case the petitioner being a major son is entitled for the compensation in accordance with his dependency.

No doubt, both the claimants are grown up and self- dependent but that does not mean or can be construed that they did not suffer any loss on account of sudden loss of both of their parents.
